definition: Colloquial means characteristic of informal, everyday conversation.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word colloquial. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know colloquial should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The coach's interviews are cheerfully colloquial — 'we got out-hustled, plain and simple' — and the beat writers quote him word for word.
Relaxed is milder than colloquial — a relaxed tone loosens the collar a little, while colloquial wording belongs fully to everyday speech.
Slangy goes further than colloquial: colloquial phrasing is everyday language nearly everyone shares, while slangy expressions belong to an in-group and can shut outsiders out.

Conversational describes anything pitched like everyday talk — a tone, a pace, an easy back-and-forth between speakers. Colloquial is the sharper label: it marks the particular words and phrasings that belong to informal speech itself, so a tone can be conversational while a single word is colloquial.

Folksy is homespun and familiar on purpose — a rocking-chair warmth that can shade into performance, as when a politician plays up small-town charm. Colloquial carries no such act: it simply names wording that belongs to ordinary, everyday conversation, with no performance implied.

Translating her grandmother's letters, Mai kept the colloquial endearments as they were — 'little rice grain,' 'walk slowly now' — because scrubbing them into formal English would have lost the everyday voice that made the letters hers.
Colloquial describes register, not correctness: colloquial wording is what relaxed conversation sounds like, and it is wrong only where the setting demands formality.
It is also broader than slang — 'kids' is colloquial and universal, while true slang belongs to an in-group and dates fast.
Colloquial is the neutral, precise label for everyday spoken wording — use it when 'informal' feels vague and 'slangy' overshoots.
In a lab report or a court filing, colloquial phrasing is the thing to flag; over the dinner table, it is simply how people talk.
